q-48810.name: Question 1
q-48810.problem: Given that $r=-2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta $ for $\theta =\theta (t),$ and that$\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=3$ at the point where $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6},$ find $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.$
q-48810.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =-2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(r) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(-2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=3$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6},$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot 2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ 3 & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (2{csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})) \\ 3 & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (2\cdot 4) \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Given that r=−2cot⁡θ for θ=θ(t), and thatdrdt=3 at the point where θ=π6, find dθdt.

a
3
b
38
c
−38
d
34
e
−34
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Differentiating the given relation with respect to t using implicit differentiation, we get

r=−2cot⁡θddt(r)=ddt(−2cot⁡θ)drdt=dθdt⋅ddθ(−2cot⁡θ)drdt=dθdt⋅(2csc2⁡θ).

Now we can substitute the given information drdt=3 and θ=π6, and solve for dθdt. We get

drdt=dθdt⋅2csc2⁡θ3=dθdt⋅(2csc2⁡(π6))3=dθdt⋅(2⋅4)dθdt=38.

q-115780.name: Question 2
q-115780.problem: A particle $P$ is moving along the curve $y=7{x}^{3}+5x$ such that the $x$-coordinate of $P$ is changing at the rate of $3\,\text{m}/\text{h}.$ Find the rate of change of the $y$-coordinate when $x=1\,\text{m}.$
q-115780.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =7{x}^{3}+5x \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(7{x}^{3}+5x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7{x}^{3}+5x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (21{x}^{2}+5).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=3\,\text{m}/\text{h}$ and $x=1$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =3\cdot (21\cdot {1}^{2}+5)\,\text{m}/\text{h} \\  & =78\,\text{m}/\text{h}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-115780.html:
Question 2
?

A particle P is moving along the curve y=7x3+5x such that the x-coordinate of P is changing at the rate of 3m/h. Find the rate of change of the y-coordinate when x=1m.

a
78m/h
b
23m/h
c
76m/h
d
52m/h
e
26m/h
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Differentiating the given relation with respect to t using implicit differentiation, we get

y=7x3+5xddt(y)=ddt(7x3+5x)dydt=dxdt⋅ddx(7x3+5x)dydt=dxdt⋅(21x2+5).

Now, we can substitute the given information dxdt=3m/h and x=1 and get

dydt=3⋅(21⋅12+5)m/h=78m/h.

q-342717.name: Question 3
q-342717.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta +2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(r) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\,(\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta +2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }\,(\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta +2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot ({sec}^{2}⁡\theta -2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=-\frac{1}{3}$ and $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3},$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot [{sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})-2{csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})] \\ -\frac{1}{3} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (4-\frac{8}{3}) \\ -\frac{1}{3} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{4}{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
